CAR-E

Concept design for multimodal interactions in an autonomous vehicle

Brief

The Multimodal Interaction module gave us a set of scenarios for an autonomous vehicle. I chose this one:

An occupant needs to get out on a congested city street. The car reads the traffic around it and times the door release. Which visual, auditory and haptic cues make opening the door and stepping out safe and pleasant?

From there, I defined the situation, place, passengers and constraints, and designed the multimodal interactions around them.

The vehicle

Seats

CAR-E

AI assistant

CAR-E sits on the dashboard and is the car’s voice and face. It understands natural speech and reads gestures alongside voice, so it grasps what the driver means, not just what they say. It speaks through zoned speakers and shows where its attention is through its eyes.

  • Glow ring
  • Dynamic eyes

Command hierarchy

CAR-E listens to everyone in the car, reading natural speech and gestures together to understand what people mean. But it does not obey everyone equally. Who is speaking, where they sit and what the request affects decide whether CAR-E acts, asks, or waits. The goal is to keep the driver’s attention on the road.

  1. 1

    Driver

    Gives direct orders and has the final say. CAR-E keeps questions for the driver to a minimum.

  2. 2

    Co-passenger

    Gives direct orders inside the cabin. Driving and route changes are confirmed with the driver for safety. First person CAR-E asks when a request comes from the back.

  3. 3

    Rear passengers

    Requests are routed according to what they affect, so the driver is disturbed only when needed.

  4. Recognised profiles

    Facial recognition links a face to a profile. A profile can be allowed to control its own zone directly, like the driver’s child turning on the rear AC.

Request typeDriverCo-passengerRear passengerRecognised rear passenger
Driving and routeStop, pull over, change destinationActs directlyConfirms with driverConfirms with driverConfirms with driver
Shared cabinMusic, front climate, windows, displayActs directlyActs directlyAsks co-passenger, then driverAsks co-passenger, then driver
Own zone comfortRear AC, reading light, sunshadeActs directlyActs directlyAsks co-passenger, then driverActs directly
Doors and exitDoor release, child lock, exit sideSensors decideSensors decideSensors decideSensors decide
  • Acts directly
  • Asks co-passenger, then driver
  • Confirms with driver
  • Sensors decide

When someone in the back asks

  1. 1

    Rear request

    A passenger in the back speaks, points or gestures.

  2. 2

    Read the request

    CAR-E identifies who is asking and what the request affects. Driving requests go straight to the driver.

  3. 3

    Ask the co-passenger

    Eyes and voice turn to the front passenger seat, away from the driver.

  4. 4

    Then the driver

    Only if the co-passenger does not respond.

The solution is told as a story, so every interaction is seen in the moment it matters.

Marine Drive

Driving along Marine Drive, a child in the back seat spots a bhelpuri stall and asks to stop. The car hears the request, confirms it with the driver and pulls over safely. It guides the driver out on the road side, while the mother and child step out towards the promenade. Once everyone is out, the car drives off to park itself.

Rohan, in the back seat, spots a bhelpuri stall on the promenade and asks for bhel.

CAR-E picks up that the voice came from the back seat, that Rohan is sitting there, that he is pointing at the chaat stall on the promenade and that he wants bhel.

Input

  • Voice (speech)
  • Gesture
  • V2X

Gesture

CAR-E tells the driver it heard a request and asks whether it should stop.

Output

  • Speech and chime
  • Haptics (seat vibration)

CAR-E takes the driver’s spoken reply and keeps driving. The driver’s instruction overrides Rohan’s request.
